messages:
sam-infra: Heads-up — customer ACME Corp reports traffic to our hosted inference endpoints intermittently failing. They use a chained outbound proxy (corporate proxy -> security inspection -> internet) and strict outbound rules. They asked for an allowlist + notes about port mapping and hostname behavior. Any quick checklist we should give them?

jess-enginfra: Short checklist: 1) Allow outbound TCP 443 to our egress hostnames/IPs, 2) Allow DNS to resolve our hostnames (UDP/TCP 53), 3) Ensure proxy does not strip SNI/authorize TLS passthrough, 4) Preserve/allow CONNECT for HTTPS. :white_check_mark:

ryan-sre: Also call out NAT rotation — if they're allowlisting SNAT IPs they need to expect occasional changes unless they pin. Recommend hostnames instead of IPs when possible. If they must use IPs, give them ranges and a note on TTL.

priya-network: Important: Chained proxies often rewrite or inject `Proxy-Authorization` headers and may terminate TLS for inspection. If TLS-inspect is enabled, cert pinning will break. Ask if they have TLS inspection; if so we need to provide guidance for trusting our CA / using an outbound bypass for inference traffic.

sam-infra: Good point. Can we share a minimal test they can run from inside their network to verify connectivity?

jess-enginfra: Yep, this is what I usually send:
```
# DNS resolution check
nslookup api.redwood-inference.com

# HTTPS CONNECT test to verify proxy allows tunneling
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood-inference.com/healthz
```
Include note: replace host with their regional host.

ryan-sre: Add healthcheck ports: we serve control plane and runtime traffic on 443. For hosted regions we also have telemetry/metrics endpoints to 443 as well — customers often forget egress to telemetry if they lock destination ports.

priya-network: If they map outbound ports (e.g., only 443 allowed but proxy maps 443->8443), we need the proxy to preserve TLS host header/SNI. If the proxy rewrites destination port, the TLS SNI still needs to match our certs. Otherwise TLS handshake will fail.

sam-infra: Any example wording for the allowlist email? Keep it short for support team.

jess-enginfra: Draft: "Please allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) and HTTPS (TCP 443) to our regional hostnames: api.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com. If your environment requires IP allowlisting, please allow the published egress ranges (we will provide a CSV) and plan for occasional rotation — use automation to pull our prefix list. Ensure your outbound proxy supports HTTPS CONNECT and preserves SNI and Host. If your proxy performs TLS interception, add our CA to your trust store or configure a bypass for inference traffic."

ryan-sre: + add: "If you use an outbound NAT with sticky sessions, keep a 5 minute tolerance for affinity drop during maintenance. If you see 502/503s during NAT churn, this is expected until new sessions warm up."

priya-network: For customers that need L4 load-balancer source IP preservation (some on-prem appliances need origin IP), suggest enabling PROXY protocol or passing X-Forwarded-For via the proxy if your chain supports it. But note: we do not rely on client source IP for auth — we use TLS+API key.

sam-infra: Perfect. I'll send that. One more: they asked about making specific firewall rules for long-polling streaming responses. Anything special?

jess-enginfra: Streaming uses normal HTTPS long-lived connections — recommend higher idle timeout on proxies/load balancers (>= 5 minutes) and allow `Connection: keep-alive` behavior. If their proxy forcibly closes idle sockets at 1m this will kill streams.

ryan-sre: Also suggest allowing `TCP FIN` and normal ephemeral ports back to the proxy. Nothing special beyond TLS + longer timeouts.

deploy-bot: deploy #infra-notes 1869123460:published allowlist_guidance_for_chained_proxies.md

sam-infra: Thanks all — I'll attach the CSV of our published IP prefixes and the short test commands. Closing the thread after I send the note to support. :thumbsup:
